comments.author: @kangsungho9
comments.text: Thank you for this wonderful travel guide to South Korea. The video covers many of Korea’s major tourist attractions, but there are also many fascinating places that are less known to international visitors. I would especially recommend Ganghwa Island, near Seoul, which offers a rich combination of Korean history, culture, and views toward North Korea. The DMZ areas in Paju or Cheorwon are also unique places where visitors can learn about Korea’s division and hopes for peace. Boryeong, famous for Daecheon Beach (Mud Festival in summer), as well as Gongju and Buyeo, the historic centers of the ancient Baekje Kingdom, are also well worth visiting.

comments.text: Chinese phones have long been purchased by low-income consumers worldwide thanks to their affordability; however, if rising labor and component costs drive up their prices, they will likely cease to sell. While ordinary consumers have traditionally bought these phones for around $70.73, prices have recently been on the rise. The issue is that their primary appeal was their low cost; if the price point matches that of products from countries with greater reliability, there is no longer any compelling reason to choose the Chinese option. It is human nature to prefer products from more reliable nations when prices are comparable, and since these Chinese products rely on government subsidies to sell, they struggle to compete without that financial support.
